title: Cherrywood Chicken with Cranberry-Maple Gravy
description: Cherrywood perfumes the cranberries before a covered braise turns the fruit and chicken juices into a smooth maple gravy.
equipment: Immersion blender and deep heatproof jug

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs
ingredients.note: Use plain, unenhanced poultry. Remove visible fat before weighing.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain chicken-and-water broth without a vegetable blend or added seasoning.

steps.title: Heat the pellet smoker
steps.text: Load the Traeger Silverton 610 with cherry wood pellets. Preheat with the lid closed to 300°F, allowing about 15 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the berries
steps.text: Combine {berries} and {cider} in the Dutch oven on the grate. Leave the pot open and the smoker lid closed for 15–20 minutes, until the fruit begins to split.

steps.title: Warm the broth
steps.text: Heat {broth}, {maple} and {cinnamon} to a simmer in the HexClad, then pour over the warm berries.

steps.title: Braise the thighs
steps.text: Unfold {chicken} into a single layer in the hot liquid and spoon some over the top. Cover the pot immediately as the wrap point. Braise at 300°F for 25–40 minutes, checking from 20 minutes until every thigh reaches 175°F.

steps.title: Rest in the braising liquid
steps.text: Transfer the chicken and a ladle of its liquid to a warm bowl. Cover and rest for 5 minutes while finishing the sauce.

steps.title: Smooth the fruit
steps.text: Blend the braising liquid and berries in a deep jug. Press the puree through a fine sieve into the HexClad to catch the skins.

steps.title: Bind the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Whisk in the freshly stirred slurry and let it bubble gently for 1 minute, stirring until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Sauce and serve
steps.text: Slice the rested thighs thinly across the grain and divide between bowls. Spoon the cranberry gravy over the slices, adding their resting juices to the bowls.

notes: Sauce yield: About 1 1/2 cups for two. Make ahead: Smoke and puree the fruit a day ahead if desired. Refrigerate it promptly and return it to a simmer with the broth before adding chicken. Refrigerate shallow portions within 2 hours, or within 1 hour outdoors above 90°F. Use refrigerated leftovers within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. The berry gravy keeps sliced chicken moist for up to 2 months and thickens again with gentle stirring. Fridge reheat: Warm the sliced thighs in their gravy covered in the HexClad over medium-low with a splash of water. Stir or turn occasionally and check from 6 minutes, until the center reaches 165°F. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then follow the fridge reheating directions. Option A uses cranberries and cider. For a gentler Option B, use the same weight of peeled ripe pear and use additional plain broth in place of the cider. No dairy is needed. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/2 of recipe): 264 kcal, 29.2 g protein, 22.2 g total carbohydrate, 5.9 g fat, 1.7 g fiber, 157 mg sodium. Includes all the chicken and sauce in the listed recipe. Sodium varies with the broth. Fiber is estimated before straining.
